v: Stop translating word by word from Urdu
Start a daily 10-minute speaking habit

b.v: About 20 minutes. Speak every example out loud - reading silently does not train speaking.
Interviewers and clients do not expect perfect English. They want to understand you easily. Short, clear sentences in simple words are better than long sentences full of difficult words.

v: Instead of: 'Myself Ali, I am having 3 years experience in the sales field.'
Say: 'I'm Ali. I have three years of experience in sales.'

b.v: Step by step:|Pick one topic: your day, your job, a news story.|Speak about it for 2 minutes and record yourself on your phone.|Listen once and write down 2 mistakes.|Say those sentences again correctly.
Use Urdu voice typing's English option to see what you said written down - it shows where your pronunciation is unclear.
Do this now:|Record 2 minutes about your daily routine.|Find 2 mistakes and fix them.

v: Give a 60-second introduction
Answer 'Tell me about yourself' well

b.v: Step by step:|Present - who you are now: 'I'm an accountant at a textile company in Faisalabad.'|Past - your relevant experience: 'For three years I have handled payroll and tax returns.'|Strength - one thing you are good at, with an example: 'Last year I reduced late payments by organising a new reminder system.'|Future - why this job: 'Now I'm looking for a role in banking where I can grow.'

v: Start with your date of birth and your father's name
Read your whole CV aloud
Speak for more than about 90 seconds
I'm currently working as...
I have ... years of experience in...
I'm good at...
I'm looking for an opportunity to...

b.v: Do this now:|Write your 4-part introduction.|Say it without reading 5 times.|Record it and check it is under 90 seconds.

v: Prepare answers to the 6 most common questions
Use the STAR method for examples
Tell me about yourself.
Why do you want this job?
What are your strengths?
What is your weakness?
Tell me about a problem you solved.
Where do you see yourself in five years?
Situation - where and when
Task - what you had to do
Action - what YOU did (say 'I', not 'we')
Result - what happened, with a number if possible

b.v: Choose a real, small weakness and show what you are doing about it: 'I used to find public speaking difficult, so I joined a weekly practice group and now I present our team report every month.'
Never say 'I have no weakness' or 'I work too hard'. Interviewers hear it every day.
Do this now:|Write a STAR answer for 'Tell me about a problem you solved.'|Practise all six answers out loud once.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Talking about salary, notice and questions for them

v: Discuss salary politely
Ask good questions at the end
Find the usual range for the job first
Give a range, not one number: 'I'm looking for something between ... and ..., depending on the full package.'
If asked your current salary, answer honestly or politely focus on the new role's value
My notice period is one month.
I can join from the first of next month.
I'd need to give my current employer two weeks' notice.
What does a typical day look like in this role?
How will my performance be measured?
What are the next steps in the process?

b.v: Always have 2 questions ready. 'No questions' can sound like no interest.
Do this now:|Write your salary range sentence.|Write 2 questions for the interviewer.|Practise them with a friend.

v: Start and end calls professionally
Handle not understanding someone
Hello, this is Sana from ABC Traders. Is this a good time to talk?
I'm calling about...
Thank you for your time. I'll send you the details by email today.
Have a good day. Goodbye.
Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
Could you speak a little more slowly?
Just to confirm, you mean...?
Could you spell that, please?
Test the camera, sound and internet 30 minutes before
Look at the camera when you speak, not at your own picture
Quiet room, plain background, phone on silent

b.v: Do this now:|Role-play a 2-minute phone call with a friend: you call to ask about a job opening.|Use at least 3 phrases from today.

v: Write short, clear emails
Use the right greeting and closing

b.v: Step by step:|Subject - clear and specific: 'Leave request - 12 and 13 December'|Greeting - 'Dear Mr. Ahmed,' or 'Hi Sara,' for colleagues|Purpose in the first line|Details in short lines|Action - what you need and by when|Closing - 'Best regards, Ali Khan'

v: Could you please...?
I would be grateful if...
Please find attached...
Let me know if you need anything else.
Sorry for the delay in replying.
'Kindly do the needful' - say exactly what you need
'Respected Sir' in every email - 'Dear Mr. Ahmed' is normal
ALL CAPITALS - it reads like shouting
Long paragraphs

b.v: Do this now:|Write an email asking a supplier for an updated price list by Friday.|Keep it under 80 words.

day-7.t: Day 7 — Common mistakes Pakistani speakers make

v: Fix 10 very common mistakes
Sound more natural immediately
'I am having a car' → 'I have a car'
'He told to me' → 'He told me'
'Discuss about the plan' → 'Discuss the plan'
'I am agree' → 'I agree'
'Return back' → 'Return'
'Since 3 years' → 'For 3 years'
'Revert back to me' → 'Reply to me' / 'Get back to me'
'Myself Ali' → 'I'm Ali'
'Today morning' → 'This morning'
'What is your good name?' → 'May I have your name?'
V and W are different: 'very well' - lips touch teeth for V
Do not add a vowel before S words: 'school', not 'iskool'
'Th' in 'think' - tongue lightly between the teeth

b.v: Do this now:|Say each wrong sentence and then the correct one out loud.|Record yourself saying 'very well, thank you' and 'I think so' and check the sounds.

v: Give your opinion politely
Present a short update
In my opinion...
I see your point, but...
Could we also consider...?
I agree with Sara about...
Can I add something here?

b.v: Step by step:|What I did last week|What I will do this week|One problem and what I need

v: Speak slower than feels natural
Pause after each point
Look at people, not only at the screen
Practise the first 3 sentences until they are easy

b.v: Do this now:|Prepare a 1-minute update about your week.|Present it to a family member or record it.

v: Handle customers politely, even angry ones
Use calm, clear phrases
Good morning, how can I help you?
Let me check that for you.
Thank you for waiting.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

b.v: Step by step:|Listen without interrupting|Say sorry for their trouble: 'I'm sorry this happened.'|Repeat the problem: 'So the parcel arrived damaged.'|Offer a solution and a time: 'I'll arrange a replacement by Thursday.'|Follow up as promised

v: I'm afraid we can't do that, but we can...
Unfortunately that's not possible. What I can do is...
I understand. Let me see what options we have.

b.v: Do this now:|Role-play an angry customer with a friend.|Use all five steps.|Swap roles.
